claims.text: Controlled post-synthesis thermal annealing improves atomic-level homogeneity in noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.
Improved atomic-level homogeneity increases the density and uniformity of catalytically active sites.
Increasing the density and uniformity of active sites enhances catalytic performance relative to an unannealed material.
High configurational entropy during synthesis promotes solid-solution formation.
As-synthesized high-entropy alloy nanoparticles may retain local compositional fluctuations.
Moderate thermal annealing supplies energy for atomic interdiffusion and redistribution.
Annealing-driven interdiffusion reduces local compositional fluctuations.
Annealing aligns the electronic structures of the material more uniformly.
More uniform electronic structure enhances the density and consistency of active catalytic sites.
Annealed nanomaterials will exhibit greater phase uniformity than otherwise identical unannealed nanomaterials.
Greater phase uniformity after annealing will be evidenced by sharper XRD peaks.
Annealed nanomaterials will show more uniform elemental maps than unannealed nanomaterials.
Annealed nanomaterials will have improved catalytic performance, such as increased turnover frequency, relative to unannealed nanomaterials.
The proposed effect should hold under typical synthesis temperatures, inert atmospheres, and moderate annealing protocols.
The proposed effect should hold for catalytic reactions in which a uniform distribution of active sites is critical.
Annealing can cause particle coarsening that degrades catalytic activity.
